N° 12Farming and networking game2026

How to use Racines & Réseaux

For players who love farming and life games, members of the Cameroonian diaspora who want to know the West, Littoral and Centre regions better, and anyone curious about networking as a real trade.

Open Racines & Réseaux ↗Platform detailsContact

Guided tourReal screens

Plays automatically. Use the dots or arrows to move, Pause to stop.

01

Getting started

1

Go to racines-reseaux.vercel.app on a computer and wait for the game to load.

2

Choose New game. Settings switch the whole game between English and French and enlarge the text.

3

Move with WASD or the left stick. Press E to talk or interact, and the use key for the tool in your hand.

4

Talk to Grandpa in the courtyard. He gives you your first seeds and your first quest.

5

Open the journal to see every quest. Its buttons take you to the next step, even in towns you cannot walk in yet.

02

Features

01

Grandfather's farm

Clear the weeds and stones, till, plant, water and harvest. Crops grow overnight and the rain waters them. Sell at the roadside stand or keep the harvest for processing.

STEPS

  1. Pick the hoe, the watering can or a seed bag in the bar
  2. Use it on the tile in front of you
  3. Sleep in the farmhouse to end the day
02

The Bandjoun Kingdom

A walkable kingdom: the chefferie with its great hut and carved pillars, the edge of the sacred forest, the museum, the coffee cooperative, the raffia valley and your father's family compound with its own fields. Fifty villagers keep a daily routine.

STEPS

  1. Take the bus to Bandjoun when the story calls you
  2. Walk up to anyone and press E
  3. Offer the item in your hand as a gift
03

The eight-day market

The Bandjoun market gathers on market day of the Bamiléké eight-day week, shown at the top left. Sell your harvest and buy seeds; each market has its own prices.

STEPS

  1. Check the day name on screen
  2. Walk to a stall and press E
  3. Hold Shift to sell a whole stack
04

Artisans and processing

Workshops for the sculptor, beadwork, ndop dyeing, pottery and raffia, plus a kitchen, a drying rack and a coffee huller. Each recipe turns raw crops into products that sell for more.

STEPS

  1. Bring the ingredients
  2. Interact with the workshop
  3. Choose the recipe and wait
05

Bus travel and towns

The bus agency serves 18 towns in the West, Littoral and Centre regions, each with its fare and travel time. New towns open as the story moves on.

STEPS

  1. Go to the bus agency or the farm signpost
  2. Choose a town and pay the fare
  3. Highland produce sells higher in Douala and Yaoundé
06

Town screens

Towns without a walkable map yet open as a town screen with their markets, their people and articles to discover, like Foumban and its brass casters.

STEPS

  1. Open a market
  2. Talk to the people of the town
  3. Read about the town
07

Characters and quests

146 characters with portraits, from the Fo and the Mafo to bayam-sellam, artisans, traders, friends and family. Quests include council palavers where your choices matter, funerals, la dot, festivals and helping neighbours.

STEPS

  1. Read the active step in the top right
  2. Open the journal for every quest
  3. Use its buttons to call, attend or travel
08

Network labs

A workbench for real faults: a school with no internet, a router with no route out, a DNS mystery. You inspect devices, change settings and write a report, and the lab scores your method.

STEPS

  1. Read the brief on the notice board
  2. Inspect, then change one thing at a time
  3. Write the report to finish
09

Encyclopedia

185 articles on Bandjoun, the West, Littoral and Centre regions, crops, processing, markets, crafts, ceremonies and networking. Each article lists its sources.

STEPS

  1. Open it from the menu
  2. Pick a category or search
  3. Follow the related links
03Tips
  • Process before you sell: roasted coffee, sauce jaune and raffia chairs are worth far more than raw crops.
  • Plan big trips on market day and fill your bag first; the bus fare only pays off with a full load.
  • For the Windows version, use a gamepad if you play on a handheld PC.
04FAQ
Is it free?

Yes, the test version is free in the browser. A full release on Steam is planned.

Are the kings and notables real people?

No. Places, crops, crafts and customs are real and sourced, but every character, including the Fo of Bandjoun, is fictional.

Which languages?

English and French, with words in Ghomálá', Duala and Ewondo explained in the text.

Does it work on a phone?

It is made for a computer with a keyboard or a gamepad.

Can every town be walked?

Grandfather's farm and Bandjoun are walkable maps today. Other towns open as town screens while their maps are built.
